title: Allow empty specifier in import maps

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
Currently, import maps allow mapping of trailing `/` specifiers, but that still requires an actual specifier before the `/`, e.g.

```json
{
	"imports": {
		"foo/": "https://cdn.foo.com/dist/"
	}
}
```

Allowing an *empty* specifier permits defining catch-all URLs to resolve unknown specifiers (e.g. via a CDN) whereas right now there is no way to hook into this. And given existing resolution rules, any other rule would take precedence, so the empty specifier would only activate when the specifier would otherwise produce an error.

This would look very similar to a trailing slash mapping, e.g.:


```json
{
	"imports": {
		"": "https://esm.sh/"
	}
}
```


If I'm reading the spec right, it seems the changes that would be needed to support this would be minimal, described below.

### Proposed spec changes

Today `""` is dead twice: [normalize a specifier key](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#normalizing-a-specifier-key) drops it at parse; [resolve an imports match](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#resolving-an-imports-match) has no branch for it. Four small edits:

1. **[Valid module specifier map](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#valid-module-specifier-map)**: drop "keys must be nonempty"; require value to end in `/` if the key ends in `/` **or is empty**.
2. **[normalize a specifier key](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#normalizing-a-specifier-key)**: delete step 1 (empty → null).
3. **[sort and normalize a module specifier map](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#sorting-and-normalizing-a-module-specifier-map) step 6**: apply the slash-value check to empty keys too.
4. **[resolve an imports match](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#resolving-an-imports-match)**: in the prefix branch, also match when `specifierKey` is `""` **and `asURL` is null**. Body unchanged — `{"": "https://cdn/"}` resolves `foo` → `https://cdn/foo`.

`asURL is null` (not `null or special`) still limits the catch-all to bare specifiers, so URL-like ones still return via `asURL` instead of throwing the bare-specifier `TypeError`. Precedence and the resolved-module-set invariant need nothing extra — `""` is code-unit-least, so descending sort puts it last.

Note: scopes resolve before global `imports`, so a scoped `""` shadows global rules for unknown specifiers in that scope.

--- 

Happy to prototype a PR along these lines if this is of interest!
